text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High KV cache eviction rate detected across us-west-2. Continuous-batcher lat p50 → 420ms (+x3), error 5xx spike 2.8% 

incident-bot: Related signals: batch_window config drift, recent kernel rollout 2026-03-15T03:12:00Z, sudden IO pressure on nvme-gpu nodes. Pager triggered (sev2).

taylor: I'm on it. paging handoff: taylor (oncall) --> samir (eng-runtime) if needs patching. Ana on support for customer comms. Liz standby for infra-level knobs.

samir: seeing sustained shard-level eviction on kv-groups 12/13. per-tenant tail lat spiking for large seq_len requests. Looks like batch_window default lowered to 8ms in the kernel change. Trying to repro locally.

liz: adding node-level throttles to reduce prefetch pressure. Will flip prefetch backoff stage to 2.

taylor: Per runbook, if cache blowup -> try per-customer throttle before global rollback. Which tenants are hottest?

ana: top impacted customers: acme-corp (25% of spike), nova-data (13%), edgepilot (8%). Support is ready to notify acme if we need a brief degraded throughput window.

samir: quick mitigation plan: 1) toggle batch_window feature flag back to previous value for all hosts 2) if risky, do per-customer override for acme-corp first 3) adjust prefetch backoff on hot nodes.

taylor: I prefer per-cust override first, acme is heavy but ok with 1-2min change. samir can you push per-cust flag? I'll coordinate canary.

samir: doing per-cust override now: command ->

rkctl flags set batch_window_ms=32 --flag=batch-continuous-window --scope=tenant:acme-corp --note="hotfix per-cust evict spike 3170001234"

samir: applied to acme-corp; waiting for metrics.

deploy-bot: FLAG UPDATE: batch-continuous-window=32ms for tenant:acme-corp applied (hash: f9b3).

samir: metrics look promising for acme: eviction rate down 78% within 45s, p50 down to 110ms.

liz: pushed prefetch backoff stage=2 to the two hottest hosts (nvme-03, nvme-07). Will watch memory churn.

taylor: good. Let's keep per-cust override for 10m, then evaluate global rollback if other tenants remain impacted. Ana, can you ping acme support with a short heads-up? Mention low-level throttle being applied and expected improvement.

ana: pinged acme support channel: "we're observing cache pressure on your workload; applied a temporary config that should reduce evictions. Let us know if you see regressions." They replied: "thx, we'll monitor."

samir: other tenants still high but lower magnitude. I want to prepare a hotfix to the batch-window default in config and roll it as a canary to 5% of backends first. Patch is small: restore default 32ms, add guard to not lower below 16ms without explicit flag.

taylor: outline rollout steps in thread and then we can do staged canary. Keep per-cust overrides until global is stable. Also plan for automatic fallback if 5xx>1% during canary.

samir: rollout plan:
- create hotfix image with config bump
- deploy to canary pool (5% traffic) with auto-fallback (deploy-bot will revert on threshold)
- monitor p50/p95, eviction-rate, 5xx for 15 minutes
- promote to 25% -> 50% -> full if metrics stable

samir: building image now. ETA ~6m.

deploy-bot: DEPLOY: started canary rollout batch-hotfix-v1 -> canary-pool (5%). Auto-fallback: enabled.

liz: monitoring infra; prefetch backoff reduced disk IO on nvme nodes. If canary shows IO regression we'll pause.

taylor: timeboxed checks at +2m, +7m, +15m. If anything crosses thresholds we revert. Ana keep ACME in the loop.

samir: canary metrics at +7m: p50 improved 25%, evictions down 60% across canary. 5xx stable at 0.6%. Looks safe to proceed to 25%.

deploy-bot: DEPLOY: promoted batch-hotfix-v1 -> 25% traffic.

ana: acme support acknowledges improvement. No customer-facing incident email required for now.

liz: notices a slight CPU bump on canary hosts but within headroom. Still ok.

taylor: proceed to 50% after 10m if stable. Samir, add automated post-deploy check to ensure no tenant-specific regressions (run per-tenant smoke using curl to typical seq_len 1024 paths).

samir: added smoke script and scheduled probe. Running now.

samir: smoke results show nova-data has a minor p95 bump (10%). I'm keeping nova-data on per-cust override for now as we push global. I'll set tenant:nova-data batch_window back to the previous value until we can investigate route patterns.

taylor: agree. Do per-cust for nova-data. Keep rollout but mark as partial due to known exceptions.

samir: applied override for nova-data.

deploy-bot: FLAG UPDATE: batch-continuous-window=16ms for tenant:nova-data applied (hash: d2a7).

liz: I'm writing an infra follow-up to investigate kernel rollback and why window ended up lowered in the first place. We should add gating in CI for batch config diffs.

taylor: post-incident tasks: 1) Document canary thresholds and auto-fallback knobs (samir) 2) Add CI gate for batch_window diffs (liz) 3) Support comms template (ana) 4) Run replay with nova-data workload (samir + infra). I'll take ownership of the incident summary and tag for postmortem.

ana: acknowledging. I'll draft customer note for acme and nova if needed.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress. Current state: per-cust overrides applied for acme-corp and nova-data; global canary at 25% progressing to 50%. No broad customer outage. Severity downgraded to sev3 pending RCA.

samir: final note: kept per-cust overrides in place until full rollout done and we validate memory/IO pressure across all regions. Will start a focused regression test for seq_len 2048 soon.

liz: if no regressions in next 30m, we'll promote to full and remove temporary overrides. I'll join postmortem tomorrow.

taylor: thanks everyone. Handoff: I'll be the incident owner for wrap-up. If anything new crops up, page oncall for immediate triage.
